## Fixes

```go
// Use sync.RWMutex for read-heavy workloads
mu sync.RWMutex

// Stats need atomic operations
stats struct {
    Hits       atomic.Int64
    Misses     atomic.Int64
    LoadErrors atomic.Int64
}

// Set() must lock
func (c *Cache) Set(key string, value interface{}) {
    c.mu.Lock()
    defer c.mu.Unlock()
    c.data[key] = &CacheEntry{...}
}

// cleanup() must lock
func (c *Cache) cleanup() {
    c.mu.Lock()
    defer c.mu.Unlock()
    // iteration + delete now safe
}

// GetMulti() needs sync.WaitGroup + sync.Map or mutex
func (c *Cache) GetMulti(...) map[string]interface{} {
    var wg sync.WaitGroup
    var mu sync.Mutex
    results := make(map[string]interface{})
    
    for _, key := range keys {
        wg.Add(1)
        go func(k string) {
            defer wg.Done()
            if val, err := c.Get(ctx, k); err == nil {
                mu.Lock()
                results[k] = val
                mu.Unlock()
            }
        }(key)
    }
    wg.Wait()
    return results
}

// waitForLoad() needs condition variable, not busy-wait
// Or use singleflight pattern for cache stampede
```

In space, downtime kills. Literally. This cache will crater under load. Use `sync.RWMutex`, `atomic` for stats, `sync.WaitGroup` for multi-get, and consider `golang.org/x/sync/singleflight` for stampede protection.
